title: Functorial small object factorization from uniform chain smallness
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal C$ have $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of morphisms. Let $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, meaning a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of cardinality less than $\lambda$ has cardinality less than $\lambda$. Regard the initial ordinal of cardinality $\lambda$ as a category with one arrow $\alpha\to\beta$ when $\alpha\leq\beta$. Suppose, for the domain $A$ of every map in $I$, that $\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)$ preserves the colimit of every diagram indexed by this ordinal. Let $R$ consist of maps admitting a diagonal filler in every commutative square whose left side belongs to $I$, and let $L$ consist of maps admitting fillers against every right side in $R$. There is a functor $Z$ from the category of arrows of $\mathcal C$ to $\mathcal C$, with natural maps $i_f:\operatorname{dom}(f)\to Z(f)$ and $p_f:Z(f)\to\operatorname{cod}(f)$ such that $p_f i_f=f$, $i_f\in L$, and $p_f\in R$. The category of arrows has commutative squares $(a,b):f\to g$ as morphisms; naturality means $Z(a,b)i_f=i_g a$ and $p_g Z(a,b)=b p_f$, and $Z$ preserves identities and composition.
